rows.assessment: Rough headward/tailward separation follows the down-left body axis, but tail_head8 falls on the adjacent white-backed calf; withers1 lies near the lowered head/rail rather than shoulder junction. Not a reliable complete anatomical warp.

Shoulder0/2 points lie toward the lower neck, but withers1, hip/pin/tail landmarks cluster near the top rump. Midline anatomy collapses despite a mostly visible long torso.

Center_back3 is in background above the animal; withers1 and other shoulder points sit outside the right/lower body. Several rump points plausible, but full layout is inconsistent with the bent side-view target.
Several shoulder/withers/center points lie on the left wall/background outside the calf; tail point is nearer the upper rump. Occlusion persists and the full warp is unreliable.
Landmarks scatter from top rump to turned neck; withers1 and tail_head8 nearly coincide on midbody. No consistent shoulder-to-tail ordering despite visible head direction.

Most midline/hip/pin points collapse at the upper rump; withers1 is also above that rump although headward direction was down. One hip point lies on right background/gate. Shoulder pair alone does not establish usable pose.
Points cluster along right body edge; center_back3 is outside above/right. Withers/tail are near one another despite head at top and hindquarters below. Compact lying posture remains ambiguous.
Some pin/tail points occupy upper rump, but other hips and midline points sit at the lower head or on left wall. Target roughly spanned but anatomical roles are inconsistent.

Many landmarks land at or above the image top edge; head/tail were not visibly definable beforehand. Severe truncation prevents anatomical validation; retain as unresolved rather than infer missing parts.
Withers1 appears far outside the target on straw; center_back3 and hip_connector5 lie on the adjacent white animal. Strong neighbor/background contamination.
Some rump points are near the actual rump, but hips4/5 sit on the separate left animal; withers1/center3 are background above. Bent neck/side view is not reliably represented.
Tail/pin cluster partly follows upper rump, but withers1 and hip_connector5 move onto the adjacent calf. Other hip points occupy lower gate/head; full anatomy is inconsistent.
Box was preidentified as mixed. Points distribute across both adjacent calves, with center_back3 down at the head/gate and withers1 on the upper neighboring rump. Target ownership remains ambiguous.
Most landmarks shift onto the neighboring white calf left of the selected narrow body; this is not target-specific pose.
Withers/center/hip/pin/tail cluster at upper rump although target faces down. Other points extend to bottom/right background. Isolated target still lacks consistent anatomy.

conclusion: Native pose is not ready for canonical coat matching on these exposed crowded calf crops. Layouts include background/neighbor landmarks, collapsed anatomical roles and truncation. No confidence threshold, orientation search, exclusion or biological naming was attempted. The qualitative review does not produce a landmark accuracy score.
